title: Leo Snub Mosley and his slide saxophone
summary: He describes trombonist Snub Mosley, the only player of the slide saxophone, who played for the Queen of England.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Leo "Snub" Mosley. A trombonist. He was through here about a month and a half ago. "Snub" Mosley played trombone and the slide saxophone. He is the only living person in the world today who plays a slide saxophone.

Yes, sir. It's got a round bell like this. And this -- the bell's big here, and it comes up small like here, see. And it's got holes in it, see. It's got holes in it. And there's a slide that goes up, see. And it's got a crook in it, see. And they blows it and it sounds like a soprano saxophone, see. But you get your tone from sliding it up and down. And this horn must have come out, oh, back in the 20's and it never was popular, see. And I think Snub bought the last one that the factory had made before the factory went out of business.
And he was here. He's got a lot of nerve. He's an extrovert, this guy. He'll take his horn out and play it anywhere, see. And my brother and I -- when I see him, he was just

passing through, going back to New York. He had been to Little Rock to see his father. And he stopped. He was sitting at the airport and we saw him. He pulled his saxophone out and played a little tune for us, you know. And people started gathering around. Then he gave us pictures where he had played tunes for the Queen of England this past summer during the Centennial -- you know what I mean. I think she had visited up in Harlem. I think it was at Aaron Burr's home or someone's home up in Holland there.

And the Queen had it roped off. And Snub Mosley played this solo to her, and she shook his hand, see. He gave me a picture. I should have brought that picture along with me. I would like for you to have seen it, see.
Does he still play that slide saxophone?

Oh, yeah. Yeah. He still plays it, yeah. That's one of his features, yeah. And he has a combo. He plays in all the smart clubs and things in, I believe, New York, New Jersey, around. He's well known in musical circles. Snub Mosley.
